A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpikingMamba work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and renamed or relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original SpikingMamba accuracy and perplexity results, neuron and SGC ablations, and activation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds plotted results in the energy–accuracy analysis, including a larger signed spike range.

M1.justification: TI-LIF is renamed SI-LIF, retaining the same signed rounding-and-clipping neuron, SGC pathway, distillation losses and DPO/KTO alignment. The revised inference derivation and newly specified implementation details do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use GenQA, InfinityInstruct and OpenHermes 2.5 for distillation and UltraFeedback for alignment. Evaluation retains the same six commonsense tasks and WikiText-2, WikiText-103, C4 and PTB. The added spike-range configuration does not expand task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Mamba2, BiLLM, Bi-Mamba, GPTQ, GPT2 and spiking-language-model baselines in Tables 2–4 and 13. SpikingBrain is newly discussed as related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: New Figure 3 includes a 1.3B signed-range ±8 configuration and explicitly excludes SGC throughout the tradeoff comparison. The retained benchmark metrics, training settings and analytical energy protocol are unchanged; moving the experimental setup into Section 5.1 does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds an energy–accuracy analysis across neuron ranges and model scales, extending the existing comparisons with a ±8 setting. Earlier neuron, SGC, loss and activation-distribution analyses remain, including the matched appendix figures.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for benchmark performance. The added tradeoff figure uses point estimates, and the existing activation-distribution reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are unchanged, including 54.62% distilled accuracy, 57.17% after KTO and the 4.7627 energy ratio. Figure 3 adds the 1.3B ±8 result and plotted 130M LIF/I-LIF accuracies; these are additional configuration results, not improvements to the retained headline results.

T1.justification: Equation 9 revises the reconstruction algebra: v1 applies the input sign outside the projected sum, whereas v2 places input-specific signs inside the projection and expands signed column accumulation. This is a limited mathematical correction, although the final event-sum expression still omits an explicit outer micro-timestep sum.

C1.justification: The central contributions and headline claims remain signed spike encoding, training-only SGC, efficient distillation and further improvement through alignment. The abstract's added 2.23-point remaining gap restates the already reported 4.78-point gap minus the 2.55-point improvement.

C2.justification: The new tradeoff discussion interprets wider signed ranges as increasing representational capacity while reducing the energy ratio, and explicitly acknowledges increased inference latency with larger D. Existing explanations of SGC, alignment benefits and activation polarization are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, specifies surrogate-gradient slope α = 1, and gives exact SGC layer indices for both model sizes. It also replaces the explicit NVIDIA A100 identification with generic BF16 accelerators rated at approximately 312 TFLOPS, reducing hardware specificity without establishing a hardware change.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to CLIF, Meng et al. (2023) and SpikingBrain, while removing Wu et al. (2018). The new SpikingBrain passage distinguishes inference-oriented integer activations from end-to-end training; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 reworks the introduction and related work, adds notation explanations and numbered subsections, and renames TI-LIF to SI-LIF. The experimental setup moves from v1 Appendix C to Section 5.1. The overall section sequence and most method, results and conclusion prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the energy–accuracy scatterplot as Figure 3, updates neuron labels and captions, resizes Tables 3–4, and adds publication headers and colored cross-references. Existing appendix plots are retained and relocated or renumbered, rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Explicit surrogate-gradient and SGC-layer settings, clearer explanations, a code-access link and the additional spike-range analysis modestly improve reproducibility and assessment of the tradeoff. The principal empirical evidence remains unchanged. Less specific hardware disclosure and incomplete final notation in Equation 9 limit the gains, but do not outweigh these documentation and analysis improvements.
